---
title: "AprilTag tracking on Quest 3 in eight diagrams"
subtitle: "Technical paper series"
---

**English** · [Deutsch](uebersicht.html){hreflang=de lang=de}

The series follows a measurement from the corners of a tag in a camera image to its motion in WebXR space. Each paper addresses a physical question, derives the equations used by the implementation and shows how to check the result. All eight chapters are available as working drafts. The reference describes release **v1.4.0** (27 November 2026).

**Reading the results.** Tag edge lengths and target coordinates set the metric scale. Choose the matching rig and verify the printed or displayed dimensions at 1:1. Calibration estimates the camera model and timing. The native anchor defines the origin for one XR session. An optical pose comes from a camera observation. A hand-driven or predicted pose can update on intervening XR frames. [Target sizes and IDs](https://github.com/PiMaV/Quest3-WebXR-AprilTag/blob/v1.4.0/docs/markers.md)

| Diagram | Question |
|---|---|
| **01 · [Calibration](01-calibration.html)** | How can head motion around a stationary target reveal both the rigid camera-to-head transform and the time offset between the camera and WebXR? |
| **02 · [World origin](02-world-origin.html)** | When do optical estimates of the target’s position and orientation agree closely enough to establish an XR anchor? |
| **03 · [Single-tag tracking](03-single-tag.html)** | How do four image corners and a known edge length determine a metric pose? How can the tracker detect an implausible jump? |
| **04 · [Multi-tag tracking](04-multi-tag-focus.html)** | How should the detector allocate search windows and processing time across tags that differ in speed and visibility? |
| **05 · [Hand coupling](05-hand-coupling.html)** | How can a measured hand-to-object offset carry the object pose forward, and when does the rigid-coupling assumption break down? |
| **06 · [Prediction](06-prediction.html)** | How far can position and orientation be extrapolated from recent optical poses while waiting for the next observation? |
| **07 · [Trajectory correction](07-trajectory-correction.html)** | How does a new optical pose correct the end of a predicted trajectory segment, and how is the correction distributed over earlier points? |
| **08 · [Perimeter](08-perimeter.html)** | How do markers on a tabletop define the vertices of a spatial boundary, and how does uncertainty in one vertex affect its outline? |

The [diagram collection](https://github.com/PiMaV/Quest3-WebXR-AprilTag/blob/main/docs/diagrams.md) shows how the modules fit together. [How Quest 3 finds a moving AprilTag again](index.html) connects several of them using a pendulum as an example.

## Tracking update · 27 November 2026

| Change in the local revision | Where to read the details |
|---|---|
| Focused submissions move from the old 28 Hz ceiling to 60 Hz. Foreground crops and periodic wide sweeps have different costs. | [Camera cadence, detection time and hits per tag](04-multi-tag-focus.html) |
| Carried tags tolerate faster head turns. The optical predictor stays active during hand coupling and takes over at release. | [Motion gates](03-single-tag.html) · [Hand-to-optical handover](05-hand-coupling.html) |
| A 100 ms old observation at 1 m/s advances 90 mm under the current predictor, previously 72 mm. | [Prediction equations and limits](06-prediction.html) |
| Removal of a missing perimeter marker depends on effective image resolution, ROI coverage and time in view. | [Perimeter visibility](08-perimeter.html) |

The rates above are configuration limits. The recorded hardware benchmark of 89–90 FPS covers the XR anchor loop. A before/after Quest measurement of fresh optical hits per second is still outstanding.
